clue.text: Writing letters to shop, I got a reply, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that these words turn up in an unexpected new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A customer writes to a shop and is startled to get an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' signals rearranging SHOP I GOT A REPLY; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistolography is the art or practice of composing correspondence.

clue.text: Ruined fort in disorder is the minister's responsibility

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked fort goes inside the disorder

parts.note: polio is a disease, a bodily disorder

indicators.note: a ruined fort is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crumbling fort in a sorry state falls under some government minister's remit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' scrambles the fort, and 'in' sets the result within the disease, just after its first letter. 'disorder' looks like a second anagram signal but is the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the government department or area of duty they hold.

clue.text: Attempt to discredit medical sample

definitions.meaning: a slur campaign against someone's reputation
cells taken on a swab, as in a cervical test

explanation.definitionFit: A smear is both a slander campaign and a scraping of cells taken for testing.

clue.text: Golden threads ensnaring a number of musicians

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: ensnaring means one piece traps the other inside it

parts.note: threads of an argument are its gists, its main points

explanation.surface: Gold strands somehow entangle a group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensnaring' traps 'a number' within the threads; 'Golden' is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Organists are musicians who play the church keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Order to take more Italian drug

indicators.note: to take means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
piu is Italian for more, familiar from musical directions like piu mosso

explanation.surface: An instruction to swallow an extra dose of some Italian narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is the container signal; the Order of Merit is a British honour, and piu is the Italian from music.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic obtained from poppies.

clue.text: Nag girl about popular worker

indicators.note: about means the girl's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
in means fashionable or popular
an ant is the crossword's classic worker

explanation.surface: Nag a girl about some well-liked employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'Nag' looks like a verb but is a noun: Don Quixote's broken-down horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is Don Quixote's scrawny old horse, the name now used for any worn-out hack.

clue.text: Recipient of agreement during exercise

indicators.note: during means the agreement sits inside the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
aye is a vote of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone who got a deal while working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal; school PE is the exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the person to whom money is paid.

clue.text: Investigative branch on its beam-end?

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London police's investigative headquarters
an arm is a branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: A department of detectives finds itself at the end of its tether.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is London police headquarters. On a ship, a yard is a spar crossing the mast, so a yardarm is the end of that beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either tip of the spar slung across a sailing ship's mast.

clue.text: Oaf keeping bridge opponents' secret

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other piece within it

parts.note: a clot is a clumsy fool
South and East are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool is hiding what the card players across the table are up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts S and E inside CLOT; bridge seats are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means private or hidden, as in a closet fan.

clue.text: At which you're free to be expansive

explanation.definitionFit: To be at large is to be at liberty, and large also means big or broad.

clue.text: Opponent in argument wins over philosopher

parts.note: wins means gains
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Someone debating comes out ahead of a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Ayer was a well-known British philosopher; 'over' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so one who does so is a contradicter.

clue.text: Spice Girl's receiving very loud backing

indicators.note: backing means the whole construction is read in the reverse direction
receiving means the girl's name holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Nora's, from the girl's name Nora
ff is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl gets very noisy support from her fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' is the container signal and 'backing' turns the whole result round. 'Spice Girl' looks like one name; 'Spice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Statesman introducing headless composer to Mum

indicators.note: introducing one piece to another here means putting it inside

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: headless means the composer loses his first letter

parts.note: Handel is the German-born composer

explanation.surface: A politician brings a decapitated composer to meet his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' drops the composer's first letter, and 'introducing' sets what is left within Mum's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was the South African statesman and president.

clue.text: Such a glass shows the insolence of organised labour

parts.note: TU is a trade union, organised workers
lip is cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: A wine glass seems to reflect the cheek of the unions.
explanation.walkthrough: TU (trade union) and LIP come in the other order in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip glass has a bowl shaped like the flower, used for wine or beer.

clue.text: Joke with hard black hood about drink container

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: about means the hood goes round the other letters

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A jest involving a dark, tough hood and something to drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the pencil letters for hard and black within the monk's hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbowl is a large bowl for serving mixed drinks at a party.

clue.text: Mutt's in or out of element

indicators.note: out of here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is taken as its letters MUTTS

explanation.surface: Is the dog in or out of its natural element?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' signals rearranging MUTTS IN OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Strontium is a metallic chemical element, number 38.

clue.text: Sway measuring sticks with it

parts.note: rulers are measuring sticks
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Moving gently, holding some rulers in fashionable style.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway as a noun means control or power, as in holding sway.

clue.text: Fishy compiler gets told off about old solver's ring

parts.note: the compiler, the setter, refers to himself as I

indicators.note: about means the scolding word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold
thy is the archaic form of your, the solver's
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A suspicious setter is scolded over the solver's old ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; chid is an archaic past tense and thy archaic 'your'. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichthyoid means fishlike, from the Greek word for a fish.

clue.text: Setter carrying ammunition? It's a plant

indicators.note: carrying means the setter holds the ammunition inside

parts.note: gel is something that sets
rounds are bullets or shells

explanation.surface: A crossword setter seems to be armed, but it's just a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; it is something that sets. 'carrying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Drink to source of groceries, meat and material

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: source of means just the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Spirits, groceries and cold cuts on a shopping list, plus some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes G from 'groceries'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric.

clue.text: Thin air in the Netherlands

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: The thin atmosphere of the low-lying Dutch country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'the Netherlands'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was the old name for the upper sky or the rarefied substance once thought to fill space.

clue.text: Climbing hill to catch up and get off

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the hill word reads upwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill on Dartmoor

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the catch word reads upwards

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A climber on a hill trying to catch up before getting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns TOR into ROT and 'up' turns NET into TEN. 'and get' is a link: food that is off has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is spoiled or decayed.

clue.text: Keeps score, though it's not much of a game

indicators.note: much of means most of the word, so it loses its final letter

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Keeping a tally, though the match hardly counts as a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' cuts the last S from CHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Notching a score is tallying it, from cutting marks in a stick.

clue.text: Island that's more than half-apprehensive

indicators.note: more than half means just over half the word is kept, losing the end

parts.note: timorous means fearful or apprehensive

explanation.surface: A place that's somewhat nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half' keeps five of the eight letters of TIMOROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Timor is a Southeast Asian island divided between Indonesia and East Timor.

clue.text: Enthusiasts going up to university cause chaos

indicators.note: going up, in a down clue, means the word reads upwards

parts.note: fans are enthusiasts

explanation.surface: Supporters arriving at university wreak havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns FANS into SNAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a muddle, and as a verb means to throw into disorder.

clue.text: The end of the computer 'acker, a one-way twister

indicators.note: the end of means the final letter of computer

parts.note: hacker with its H dropped Cockney-style; a hacker is a chopper, a hatchet, which then loses its H too

explanation.surface: A computer hacker is up to no good, twisting things one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of' takes R from 'computer'. The dropped H in ''acker' tells you to drop the H from HATCHET, a hacking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a mechanism letting a wheel or spanner turn in one direction only.

clue.text: Bird keeps Bill quiet

indicators.note: keeps means holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
AC is an account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bird keeps its beak silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is the container signal. 'Bill' looks like the bird's beak; it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or silent.

clue.text: Medical practitioner's in love, by the way

parts.note: at home means in
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A doctor is in love, by the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is short for 'is' and 'by the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeopath treats illness with tiny doses of substances.

clue.text: Split part of head

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of cleave, to split
a segment of a garlic bulb, which is called a head

explanation.definitionFit: Clove is a past tense of cleave, and a clove is a segment of a garlic bulb.

clue.text: Impure lad tutor corrupted by gross misconduct

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy tutor has led a boy astray and committed serious misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' signals rearranging IMPURE LAD TUTOR; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral turpitude is depravity, conduct contrary to good morals.
